title: NASA software classification gate
body: Software classification A (human-rated) requires: formal methods OR equivalent rigour, redundant independent implementations for safety paths, minimum 100 % MC/DC test coverage on safety-critical code, independent V&V, and operational flight heritage demonstration before crewed missions.

title: Human-rating safety risk
body: Human-rated systems shall demonstrate Loss-of-Crew (LoC) probability ≤ 1/270 for ascent, ≤ 1/270 for entry, and ≤ 1/500 for one-year orbital operations. Aggregate mission shall meet ≤ 1/200 LoC.

title: Orbital debris mitigation
body: All NASA missions in or transiting LEO shall demonstrate post-mission disposal within 25 years (passive) or active deorbit. Probability of human casualty from re-entry ≤ 1×10⁻⁴. Probability of accidental break-up during deorbit ≤ 0.001.

title: Probabilistic risk assessment scope
body: All NASA Class B+ projects shall conduct PRA encompassing crew, mission, and asset loss with quantified uncertainty bounds (5th–95th percentile). PRA results inform design changes; numerical risk targets are confirmed at every design review.
citation: NASA NPR 8705.5 Technical Probabilistic Risk Assessment Procedures

title: Reliability allocation top-down
body: Mission reliability target shall be allocated to subsystems via fault-tree analysis. Each subsystem shall demonstrate (test or analysis) achieving its allocation. No subsystem shall have reliability < 0.95 over mission duration without justified waiver.
citation: NASA-STD-8729.1A Planning, Developing and Managing an Effective Reliability Program §4

title: Environmental test margins
body: Hardware shall be qualified to acceptance environment +5 °C in temperature, +3 dB in vibration, +1 dB in shock, and equivalent margins for radiation. Acceptance retest after rework shall meet original acceptance levels.
citation: MIL-STD-1540D Test Requirements for Launch, Upper-Stage and Space Vehicles §6
